Pontius Pilate. The Roman prefect of Judea during Jesus's ministry, holding civil and military authority. He interrogated Jesus, asking "What is truth?" in a moment that encapsulates philosophical distance. According to the Gospel of John, he declared Jesus innocent three times, yet still condemned him to appease the crowd. In Matthew's account, he washed his hands of Jesus's blood, a gesture symbolizing refusal of personal responsibility. His wife warned him against condemning Jesus, claiming a troubling dream—mentioned only in Matthew. Pilate authorized the Crucifixion under pressure from Jewish leaders who threatened to report him to Caesar for harboring sedition. The inscription on the cross—"Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews"—was placed there by Pilate's order and became a permanent record of the charge against Jesus. Historical sources confirm his governorship from twenty-six to thirty-six CE and his reputation for brutal suppression of dissent.
